key_concept: Lower invertebrates such as sponges, coelenterates and flatworms have no special respiratory organs and exchange $O_2$ and $CO_2$ by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.
steps: Recall the NCERT classification of respiratory mechanisms by animal group.
Sponges (Porifera), coelenterates and flatworms are simple animals. Their cells lie close to the surrounding water, so they need no special respiratory organs.
Water flows through the canal system of the sponge, and $O_2$ and $CO_2$ diffuse directly across the body surface along their concentration gradients.
A moist cuticle is used by earthworms, tracheal tubes by insects, and gills by most aquatic arthropods, molluscs and fishes. None of these apply to sponges.
Hence sponges exchange gases by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.
final_answer: Option (1): simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
why_not_others: Moist cuticle belongs to earthworms, tracheal tubes to insects, and gills to aquatic arthropods, molluscs and fishes. Sponges have no specialised respiratory structure at all.
common_trap: Students assume that an aquatic animal must use gills, but sponges are too simple to have any respiratory organ.
time_saving_tip: Memorise the four NCERT pairs: sponges, coelenterates and flatworms use body-surface diffusion; earthworms use a moist cuticle; insects use tracheae; aquatic animals use gills.
